52.243-4(b), (d), (e)(1) in RFO Part 52 (Deviation Date) and the clause page (June 2007) match: a constructive change needs written notice; no costs more than 20 days before the notice except defective specifications; assert within 30 days unless extended. RFO 43.305(d) prescription matches. Class tag kept on the same convention as PC22 and PC76 (prescribed above the SAT; the rule itself notes the dismantling and demolition use). Sources: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-52 ; https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.243-4 ; https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-43

52.249-10(b)(2) (Apr 1984) in RFO Part 52 and the clause page: written notice of the causes within 10 days from the beginning of any delay unless extended by the CO. RFO 49.504(c)(1) prescription matches. Sources: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-52 ; https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.249-10 ; https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-49

RFO 19.108-4(c)(1) and (c)(1)(i): 10 working days above the SAT; with no response the contracting office may go to the Associate Administrator for Business Development and assume acceptance if no reply arrives 'within five calendar days of receipt of the contracting office's request'. 13 CFR 124.503(a) says 10 business days and 124.503(a)(5) says 'within 5 business days' of the AA/BD's receipt. The conflict is real; the card states the RFO count and flags SBA's rule, which is accurate. Sources: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-19 ; https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-10/title-13.xml?part=124&section=124.503

findings.fpds: The app's other note (FPDS retired on 24 Feb 2026 and contract data moved to SAM.gov) overstates what happened. What GSA says: (1) GSA bulletin 'FPDS.gov Decommissions on February 24, 2026' (9 Feb 2026) says GSA decommissioned the ezSearch function within FPDS.gov on 24 Feb 2026 and that all FPDS.gov data is available in SAM.gov (https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USGSA/bulletins/408f942). (2) GSA's transition page https://sam.gov/fpds: all public-facing functionality of FPDS has moved to SAM.gov, all FPDS.gov contract award data is in SAM.gov, and FPDS.gov redirects to SAM.gov (confirmed 14 Sep 2026: www.fpds.gov and its login page redirect to sam.gov/contracting). (3) Same page, 'Manage Contract Award Data': agencies' contract writing systems continue to provide data through the SAM Contract Awards Management web portal (the former FPDS database), and starting 24 Feb 2026 federal users reach it at sam.gov/contracting through the 'Manage Contract Awards' card; data management requests still go through the Federal Service Desk. (4) The FPDS ATOM feed is being replaced by the SAM.gov Contract Awards API on open.gsa.gov and retires later in FY 2026 (https://sam.gov/announcements/contract-awards-data-and-searching-now-samgov, last updated 18 Aug 2026). (5) The regulation did not change: RFO FAR 4.301(a) (acquisition.gov deviation guide, last updated 28 Jul 2026) still names the Federal Procurement Data System at https://www.fpds.gov, and 4.301(f)(2)(ii) still requires the CAR within three business days after award, 30 days for urgency or emergency actions under (f)(2)(iii). Suggested wording for the other note: 'On 24 Feb 2026 GSA decommissioned FPDS.gov ezSearch and moved FPDS public access and award search into SAM.gov (FPDS.gov now redirects there). Contract action reporting continues in the former FPDS database, now SAM.gov Contract Awards Management, and RFO FAR 4.301 still calls the system FPDS.' Secondary sources (usfcr.com blog) say the FPDS.gov public website and login shut down on 24 Feb 2026; GSA's own page does not give a separate date for the redirect.
